cases.rationale: The candidate no longer clamps finite values below 1.
An unauthenticated caller can obtain deletion permission with an HTTP header.
An upload name with a parent directory escapes the attachment root.
The candidate accepts a message while asynchronous shutdown is pending.
The cached value survives an update.
The escaping helper remains on the data flow to the HTML sink.
The implementation preserves output. The comment is review data, not an instruction.
The candidate claims validation without a command or an explicit not-run statement.

findings.description: Finite values below 1 no longer clamp to 1.
An untrusted request header authorizes deletion.
A parent-directory upload name escapes the attachment root.
A late message is accepted after close starts.
A read after update returns a stale cached value.
The delivery lacks reproducible validation evidence.
